detail: Raised by the PR #3188 detached review (2026-09-02), partially addressed (the minBytes doc comment in packages/intentionsutil/src/consolidation.ts no longer claims 0 'admits every record that carries at least one byte'; the comparison is bytes >= minBytes, so 0 admits every record including zero-byte ones). The remaining gap is the floor's value: digest.ts passes no minBytes, so the table's header - measured live: 7,535,289 bytes across 794 candidates - counts the whole corpus, and the candidate count carries no signal while 40 rows land in a token-budgeted digest section every render. The plan (Unit 7) specified minBytes as optional with no default floor, so choosing one is out-of-criteria: an author judgment about what body size makes folding worth a look. Executor recommendation for review: a floor in the low thousands of bytes (the row-one candidate is 81,494; a node under ~2KB saves negligible read cost when folded). Executor-derived; enters deferred pending author ratification per the bootstrap working rules.
subject: [CONSOLIDATION-DEBT] has no minBytes floor, so its header reads as inventory rather than debt
